newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Inkombank sees first ADR deal next week.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Inkombank sees first ADR deal next week.

text.p: The first deal with Inkombank's level-one American Depositary Receipts will take place at the beginning of next week, a bank spokesman said on Tuesday.
"The transaction with our bank's ADRs will most likely take place on Monday or Tuesday next week," Ilya Yakushev told Reuters.
Inkombank may sell up to three percent of its authorised capital or nine million ordinary shares with a face value of 1,000 roubles.
Bank of New York is Inkombank's depositor and ING-Bank Euroasia will be the custodian.
Inkombank plans to issue level-two and level-three ADRs, which unlike level-one receipts raise new capital, in 1997 or 1998.

Last month Inkombank, Bank Menatep and Bank Vozrozhdeniye received permission from Russia's central bank to sell their shares to foreigners. Russian banks cannot sell their shares to foreigners without central bank permission for each deal.
Bank shares are not actively traded in Russia.
